newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish president says Russia accepted NATO growth.
newsitem.headline: Polish president says Russia accepted NATO growth.

text.p: Poland's President Aleksander Kwasniewski greeted the outcome of the Helsinki summit between U.S. leader Bill Clinton and Russia's Boris Yeltsin, saying on Friday that Moscow had agreed de facto to NATO's expansion.
"I think that in this basic question, in fact, I stress in fact, Russia has agreed on the expansion of NATO," Kwasniewski said in a statement issued to Reuters by his spokesman Antoni Styrczula.
Kwasniewski, whose country sees rapid NATO entry as a top policy goal, said Poland had no objections to the readiness of the United States and NATO countries to sign a special charter with Russia.

"We think that, for a lasting system of security in Europe, such a charter between an expanded NATO and Russia and Ukraine can be very useful," Kwasniewski said in initial comments just after learning the outlines of the summit's outcome.
"We also have the impression there was a drawing closer of standpoints and that in fact the expansion of NATO is decided," Kwasniewski said.

Kwasniewski said he did not consider Poland would be a second-class member of NATO because the pact would not station nuclear weapons or forces on its territory, as it would have the same guarantees and responsibilities as other members. "So in my view the expansion of NATO in peaceful conditions is expansion in which the presence of foreign armies and nuclear weapons is not essential," he said in the statement.
